symbols.note: from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 --full; no per-method address was found in bg3_dx11.exe (null)
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Runs, in order: ProcessComponentUpdates, ProcessAbortRequests, ProcessToggleAccessorySetRequests, ProcessOverrideAparenceVisualRequests, ProcessRemoveCustomVisualOvirrideRequests, then one Update call on each of five sub-objects of the system (at offsets 0x250, 0x338, 0x438, 0x4e8, 0x588), then CleanUp. The strings in the sub-object code show 0x250 is the CreationSubsystem, 0x338 the LevelUpSubsystem, 0x438 the RespecSubsystem and 0x4e8 the ChangeAppearanceSubsystem; 0x588 is taken to be the full-respec one from its behaviour, not from a string.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll esv::character_creation::System::Update read (calls only); sub-object names from strings in EoCServer.dll+0x154CEA0 (CreationSubsystem::RequestAbort), +0x152BD80 (RespecSubsystem), +0x157C020 (ChangeAppearanceSubsystem.cpp), +0x15413A0 (LevelUpSubsystem::RequestAbort). bg3_dx11.exe+0x316C3A0 has the same call order (the survey delta between the two builds is 0x170).

does.text: Walks the abort requests and, for each entity, tests which definition component it holds and hands it to the matching sub-object's RequestAbort: LevelUpSubsystem, RespecSubsystem (+0x438), CreationSubsystem or ChangeAppearanceSubsystem (+0x4e8). For the change-appearance case the sub-object only appends the entity to its pending list; nothing is created there.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll ProcessAbortRequests read around the four dispatch calls (EoCServer.dll+0x15413A0, EoCServer.dll+0x152ADD0, EoCServer.dll+0x154CEA0, EoCServer.dll+0x157E1F0); EoCServer.dll+0x157E1F0 read whole: it only appends the entity handle to a dynamic array at sub-object+0x20. Which component each type-index test checks was not resolved to a name.

does.text: After an abort was queued, the Update of the system walks that pending list; for every entity still alive it sets a byte of a component it fetched for the entity, notifies the listeners attached to the sub-object, then adds esv::character_creation::ChangeAppearanceCancelledOneFrameComponent; the list is emptied afterwards. (Review 2026-11-14 (Opus): order corrected: the listeners are called before the add, read at bg3_dx11.exe+0x37A9D90.) So the one-frame component appears one tick after a change-appearance session of a character is aborted.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe+0x316C3A0 (Update) loop over the list at system+0x508 calls bg3_dx11.exe+0x37A9D90, whose only add helper is bg3_dx11.exe+0x37AACC0; that helper allocates in a frame storage (ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw) keyed by the global at bg3_dx11.exe+0x60D123C, which the init at +0x2ED160 ties to the GetTypeName string of ChangeAppearanceCancelledOneFrameComponent. An add, not a remove.

does.text: For each entity handled by the creation sub-object (bg3_dx11.exe+0x37908D0 calling +0x3791580), when a flag computed for the entity is set (it records whether the entity's id was found in a hash set of the sub-object) the one-frame esv::character_creation::UserAvatarCreatedOneFrameComponent is added. It receives two entity handles produced while the character was built and a 32-bit value read from the creation data. What the hash set holds (presumably the avatar being made for a user) is a guess.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe+0x3791580 read from the top and the tail: the add is the helper bg3_dx11.exe+0x3796700 (frame-storage alloc, global bg3_dx11.exe+0x60D12CC = type index of UserAvatarCreatedOneFrameComponent, same init method as above), guarded only by its third argument, which the caller sets from the hash-set lookup at the caller's lines ~193-206.

does.text: The sub-object at +0x588 creates esv::character_creation::FullRespecCancelledOneFrameComponent for each live entity on its own pending list (list at +0x5b8 in the system, the same shape as the change-appearance one), and creates FullRespecCompletedOneFrameComponent inside its third processing function when the entity passes several tests and one looked-up pointer field is null. The tests were not identified.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe+0x316C3A0 lines for +0x588 call bg3_dx11.exe+0x37AECE0 (add helper +0x37AF6A0, global +0x60D12AC = FullRespecCancelled) and bg3_dx11.exe+0x37AD930 calls +0x37AE8F0 (add helper +0x37AF540, global +0x60D12B4 = FullRespecCompleted) at a branch guarded by unnamed calls. What puts entities on the cancelled list was not looked at.

does.text: RequestAutoLevel only validates the entity handle and passes it into the LevelUpSubsystem object. The add of esv::character_creation::AutoLevelRequestOneFrameComponent is not in this system at all: its only add helper (bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DC24B0) is called from esv::party_preset::System, in the pass of ProcessPostReloadStoryEvent where an entity just received esv::exp::IncreaseExperienceRequestOneFrameComponent and holds esv::party_preset::LevelUpStateComponent. For each such entity the pass removes LevelUpStateComponent (deferred) and adds AutoLevelRequestOneFrameComponent.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DBFE40 read whole (query spec type name at +0x40D6E0 lists IncreaseExperienceRequestOneFrameComponent and LevelUpStateComponent, with the added-tag on the first); it calls bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DC24B0 (frame-storage alloc, global +0x60D122C) and bg3_dx11.exe+0x400D0A0, called with the type index of LevelUpStateComponent. Review 2026-11-14 (Opus): bg3_dx11.exe+0x400D0A0 is a deferred remove: it appends to the entity's command-buffer change list the type index with storage index 0xFFFFFFFF and allocates no component storage, the same record ECS.dll's EntityCommandBuffer::RemoveComponentUnchecked (ECS.dll+0x272B0) writes. Caller: bg3_dx11.exe+0x2DBBF80 (party_preset ProcessPostReloadStoryEvent).

does.method: full-respec cancel helper (unnamed, EoCServer.dll+0x1530910; reached from +0x1534B90 and +0x15319A0)
does.text: Part of the respec path only. Given a full-respec session, it takes the session's character; if that entity is alive it sets two bytes of a component it fetches there (helper +0x1521860, replicated - first to 0, second to 1) and adds esv::character_creation::FullRespecCancelledOneFrameComponent to the character. Then it destroys the session's definition entity and the session entity itself. By its effect this is cancelling a full respec (Withers' respec); that it runs on cancel is inferred from the component it adds, the callers were not read. Review 2026-11-14 (Opus, systems I): this is the EoCServer.dll side of the run branch's "Update (full-respec part)": the add on each live entity of a pending list; the list and its fill are still not read.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x1530910 read whole (97 lines): IsEntityAlive, writes at offsets 0 and 1, add helper +0x152C360 (SetupComponentFrameStorage/AllocRaw of the global at EoCServer.dll+0x2258EA4, whose initialiser +0x17B8C0 names it through GetTypeName<esv::character_creation::FullRespecCancelledOneFrameComponent> at +0xE9B320), two DestroyEntity calls.
